source.title: Implicit Regularization and Generalization in Overparameterized Neural Networks

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper sweeps neural-network size and measures test performance, directly testing model-wise double descent. It uses its own MLP and CNN settings rather than reporting an explicit replication.
record.gate_note: The model-size sweeps in Tables I and II report test accuracy across widths or channel counts and bear on V1. The paper does not sweep training epochs or training-set size for double descent. Background discussion and cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps MLP width on MNIST and CNN channel width on CIFAR-10, reporting train and test accuracy (Tables I, II). This bears directly on model-wise double descent (V1). No epoch, sample-size, noise, regularization or effective-complexity sweeps are reported.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say double descent was observed in both sweeps and that test error keeps decreasing beyond the interpolation threshold, supporting H4. They place the CNN peak at ch8 'near the interpolation threshold'. They suggest the second descent may be partly explained by greater availability of flat minima in larger models, though they did not measure this directly.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses model-width sweeps and test performance to examine double descent, but its architectures, datasets, and training setup are its own; the text does not establish an exact match to the original experimental recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported shape differs between the MNIST MLP and CIFAR-10 CNN sweeps.
record.problems: The MNIST MLP results do not show a clear double-descent peak. In the CNN sweep, the test-error peak occurs at channels 8, where training accuracy is 45.8%, while training accuracy first reaches 100.0% at channels 32; the peak result also has ±17.5 variability. Experiments use MNIST and CIFAR-10 and five random seeds.

untested.parts: Label-noise settings, where the original's peak is strongest; architectures other than a 4-layer MLP and a small BN-CNN; dense sweeps around the threshold.
No test error over training epochs.
No variation of label noise or regularization; no multiple peaks.
No re-expression by an effective parameter count.

missing.what: Width sweep (32–4096) on a 5,000-sample MNIST subset: test accuracy rises monotonically, 91.6% to 93.9%. All widths are above p≈n, so there is no peak and only over-parameterized improvement.

record.verdict_notes: The author's 'double descent' is largely continued improvement past interpolation. On MNIST there is no peak at all. The CNN 'peak' at ch8 is in the underfit regime, not at the 100%-train size (ch32), and has huge seed variance. No label noise was used, and the original sources show the peak is weak or absent in clean-label settings, so the absence is partly expected. Training ran 60–80 epochs with no augmentation. The paper is not one of the originals.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests model-wise behavior only on its MNIST MLP and CIFAR-10 CNN sweeps.
No test-error sweep over training epochs is reported.
No training-sample-size sweep near the interpolation threshold is reported.
Experiments use deep MLPs and CNNs only; no other model classes are tested.
The paper does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
The double-descent experiments do not vary label noise or test multiple peaks or optimally tuned regularization.
The paper does not re-express results using an effective parameter count or test whether that produces an ordinary U-shaped curve.

source_check.reason: R1–R8 show no error peak near width 32, the stated first perfect-fit width. Error decreases through this threshold. The reason should describe the sweep as approximately monotonic: error rises slightly from 3.1% at width 512 to 3.2% at width 1024.

relationships.reason: The only error bump (ch8) is at 45.8% train accuracy with ±17.5 SD. At the actual just-fit size (ch32) error is lower than all smaller models, so the peak is not at interpolation and is not reliable (R9–R14).
relationships.display_finding: The only error bump occurred at 8 channels (45.8% training accuracy, ±17.5 SD), while the first sampled perfect fit at 32 channels had 34.2% test error, below every smaller model.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R9–R14 show the error peak at channels 8 with only 45.8% training accuracy. At the first sampled perfect-fit size, channels 32, error is 34.2%, below every smaller model. Thus the peak near first fit required by V1 is absent in this tested setting; the large uncertainty at channels 8 does not establish significance or training instability.
